why: Same lines as 075, e written first. A cycle is broken by removing one link (L660-661): the optional that closes it is missing (L714-716) and memoized (L884-888), so the other optional is not. Resolving f first, that link is e's ${?f.k}: e is [y], f is ${?e}${e}, both parts [y], so [y, y]. Resolving e first, f's required ${e} still closes the cycle and is an error (typesafe/config); the order is undefined, so either [y, y] or that error is allowed (L866-881). Expecting f [y] would mean two links removed (${?e} and the outer ${?f.k}), which no order produces.
